prerequisites.title: SurveyMonkey account
prerequisites.detail: API use is limited to SurveyMonkey account owners, who become Developer Account holders.

prerequisites.title: Enterprise plan for private apps
prerequisites.detail: Creating a draft is free on any plan, but deploying a private app needs Enterprise.

prerequisites.title: Correct data center portal
prerequisites.detail: US customers use developer.surveymonkey.com; European customers use developer.eu.surveymonkey.com.

prerequisites.title: Support and account statement
prerequisites.detail: State whether users need a free or paid account from your service, and provide easily accessible support.

steps.title: Open the Developer Portal
steps.detail: Log in with your SurveyMonkey account, using the portal for your data center.
steps.done_when: You can see My Apps in the portal.

steps.title: Draft scopes, listing and app name
steps.detail: Draft the scope list, a truthful listing and an app name that avoids generic terms, versions and 'SurveyMonkey'.
steps.done_when: Scope list, listing text and app name are ready.

steps.title: Create the draft app
steps.detail: Create the app, set scopes, and register the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard. Deploy within 90 days.
steps.done_when: You hold the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Upgrade to Enterprise and deploy
steps.detail: Deploy the private app on an Enterprise plan.
steps.done_when: App is deployed and not disabled.

steps.title: Submit the app listing
steps.detail: Create the listing on the listings tab in My Apps and submit it for approval.

steps.title: Wait for SurveyMonkey approval
steps.detail: SurveyMonkey reviews the app and may ask for information or access to verify compliance.

traps.title: Draft apps expire after 90 days
traps.detail: A draft app is disabled after the 90-day draft period if not deployed.

traps.title: Private apps serve one account or Team only
traps.detail: A private app cannot be shared across customers. Public apps need approval.

traps.title: Approval can be refused
traps.detail: SurveyMonkey may reject an app on unlisted criteria, and approval does not guarantee compliance.

traps.title: Overlap with SurveyMonkey's own tools
traps.detail: Apps replicating its survey tools, white-labeling it, or not related to surveys are not permitted. Public apps should also not replicate survey tools.

traps.title: Do not resell API access
traps.detail: Selling or redistributing API access needs prior written approval. Tokens work only with the app they were issued for.

traps.title: API call limits and suspension
traps.detail: Limits may change, and excessive use can lead to suspension. Public apps show 500,000 calls per day.

traps.title: Directory listing can be removed
traps.detail: SurveyMonkey may demote or remove a directory listing for any reason.

blockers.symptom: App stops working after about 90 days
blockers.what_it_means: The draft period ended without deployment.
blockers.what_to_do: Deploy the app before the draft period ends.

blockers.what_it_means: The app failed the listed criteria or other criteria SurveyMonkey keeps.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the criteria, fix the app and listing, and resubmit.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the listing and app name against the published criteria.

blockers.what_it_means: Deploying a private app requires an Enterprise plan.
blockers.what_to_do: Upgrade the account plan, or use a public app.

evidence.answer: The callback URL Composio uses for toolkit auth is on backend.composio.dev, and your proxy redirects to it.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains its own OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack (general statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: With a Composio managed app, the developer does not need to register their own OAuth app (general, for toolkits with a managed app).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: A custom auth config lets the developer supply their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: No OAuth app registration, no credentials to manage. Create a session and start testing immediately.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are suited to building and iterating, with no OAuth app registration and no credentials to manage.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which may not include everything a developer needs (for example, write access to a specific Google API).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With a managed app, users see a Composio consent screen during OAuth rather than the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio." This is the most common reason to switch.
evidence.answer: In production, a developer generally wants users to see their own app name on the consent screen, which is the most common reason to switch from a managed app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share rate-limit quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; an own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants (for example a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app rather than a managed one.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still [white-label the Connect Link page](/docs/authentication/white-labeling-authentication#customizing-the-connect-link) with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: A developer can white-label the Connect Link page with their logo and app title without needing their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You don't have to pick one approach for all toolkits.
evidence.answer: A developer can mix approaches, using their own credentials for some toolkits and Composio managed auth for others, with each toolkit having its own auth config.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey account needed by Developer
evidence.answer: For public apps, the developer's SurveyMonkey account requirement is listed as 'Any'.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Requires approval before launching
evidence.answer: Public apps require approval from SurveyMonkey before launching.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Public apps can be listed on SurveyMonkey's App Directory after meeting certain criteria and receiving approval.
evidence.answer: Public apps can be listed in SurveyMonkey's App Directory only after meeting certain criteria and receiving approval.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: How many accounts can access the app
evidence.answer: For public apps, the number of accounts that can access the app is unlimited.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: One SurveyMonkey account or one Team
evidence.answer: Private apps are limited to one SurveyMonkey account or one Team, and private apps do not require approval before launching.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey retains the right to reject an app based on criteria not listed above.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey may reject an app based on criteria not listed in the checklist.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey has strict standards for publishing public apps.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey has strict standards for publishing public apps.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your app should have unique value and be attracting new users regularly.
evidence.answer: The app must have unique value and be attracting new users regularly.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your app should NOT replicate functionality already offered by SurveyMonkey's survey tools.
evidence.answer: The app must not replicate functionality already offered by SurveyMonkey's survey tools.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your app's name should NOT be a generic term (i.e. "Analytics"), include versioning (i.e. "App V3.0"), and/or include the word "SurveyMonkey".
evidence.answer: The app name must not be a generic term, include versioning, or include the word 'SurveyMonkey'.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your app should have at least five OAuth sign ins in the first three months.
evidence.answer: The app must have at least five OAuth sign-ins in the first three months.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: You must state if users will need a free or paid account from your service to use your app.
evidence.answer: The developer must state whether users need a free or paid account from the developer's service to use the app.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your team must provide easily-accessible app support.
evidence.answer: The developer's team must provide easily accessible app support.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: All communication should be over HTTPS using a valid SSL certificate (we value security!)
evidence.answer: All communication must be over HTTPS using a valid SSL certificate.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Listings help users gain a better understanding of your app's core functionality and scope requirements.
evidence.answer: Listings should be written honestly and truthfully, and should describe the app's core functionality and scope requirements.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Approval of your app by SurveyMonkey does not guarantee its compliance with the criteria above.
evidence.answer: Approval by SurveyMonkey does not guarantee the app's compliance with the listed criteria.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.answer: For public apps, the API call limit is 500,000 per day, and the page says limits are subject to change.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: **Limits are subject to change
evidence.answer: The page states that API limits are subject to change.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: starting at 500 calls/day ( contact sales )
evidence.answer: For private apps, the API call limit starts at 500 calls per day, with contact sales.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Who purchases user's SM accounts
evidence.answer: For public apps, the end user (not the developer) purchases the user's SurveyMonkey accounts.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey account needs to be an enduser of the app
evidence.answer: For public apps, the SurveyMonkey account must be an end user's account to use the app's functionality.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: You must state if users will need a free or paid account from your service to use your app.
evidence.answer: The developer must state whether users need a free or paid account from the developer's own service.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: All communication should be over HTTPS using a valid SSL certificate (we value security!)
evidence.answer: All communication for the app must use HTTPS with a valid SSL certificate.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Visit the listings tab in the My Apps view to create an app listing and submit it for approval.
evidence.answer: App listings for public apps are created on the listings tab in the My Apps view and submitted for approval; the page does not describe creating the OAuth app or its client ID and secret.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Eligible for the App Directory
evidence.answer: Public apps are eligible for the App Directory; private apps are not.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your app should have at least five OAuth sign ins in the first three months.
evidence.answer: The app must have at least five OAuth sign-ins in the first three months to be promoted in the App Directory.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your app should NOT replicate functionality already offered by SurveyMonkey's survey tools.
evidence.answer: The app should not replicate functionality already offered by SurveyMonkey's survey tools.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your app's name should NOT be a generic term (i.e. "Analytics"), include versioning (i.e. "App V3.0"), and/or include the word "SurveyMonkey".
evidence.answer: The app name must not be a generic term, include versioning, or include the word 'SurveyMonkey'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your first app listing should be in English, but we encourage you to make additional app listings in other languages.
evidence.answer: The first app listing must be in English; additional listings in other languages are encouraged.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey's approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Only two scopes need SurveyMonkey approval for a Public app: Create/Modify Responses (responses_write) and Create/Modify Surveys (surveys_write).

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Public apps use scopes to request permissions from app users during OAuth.
evidence.answer: Public apps request scopes from end users during OAuth, and some scopes also require the end user to hold a paid SurveyMonkey plan.
